answer: Pulse-priced identity registration: each new identity must submit a random challenge whose value is verified at a public nadir of the network's coordination graph, so an attacker's identities all converge on the same scarce relay slots. When registration requests cluster, the mechanism raises the fee per slot geometrically, forcing each sybil to bid against its own duplicates. An attacker pays the marginal price of colliding with every prior fake identity plus a quill signature from a distinct hardware source, making N identities cost N times the congestion peak rather than a flat rate.
